author: Thomas Aquinas
citation_system: pars, quaestio, articulus (e.g. I q.2 a.3 co.; I q.46 a.2 ad 7)
notes: Use the conventional pars/quaestio/articulus locator as the human citation; `co.` marks the corpus (respondeo) of an article and `ad n` the reply to objection n. There is no CTS URN for the Summa, so the work and edition identifiers are SCTA (Scholastic Commentaries and Texts Archive) resource URIs: SCTA transcribes each quaestio as its own expression, and `edition_urns` lists the canonical manifestation of each pinned quaestio. The pinned witness is the SCTA LombardPress diplomatic TEI transcription of the Leonine edition (Opera omnia, vol. 4, Rome 1888), witness `cod-cnLxE4`, by Jeffrey C. Witt, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The owner accepted this witness, including its NonCommercial-ShareAlike license and draft status, as the theology base witness on 2026-10-23 (issue #143). The transcription keeps OCR residue of the Leonine apparatus markers (stray quotation marks, `?`, `^`, `$e` for `se`, and one stray full stop in `aliud. movens`); read those as noise, not as text. Corpus Thomisticum (Leonine text, unpinned web pages) is an orientation aid only. Questions without a pinned SCTA witness may be cited from the English Dominican translation (2nd rev. ed. 1920) on New Advent, pinned as a web snapshot (#154; so far I q.105 a.5); such claims carry basis translation, and a web snapshot may not cover a range a pinned Latin witness covers.
